key_insight: Human intervention in web agents follows predictable patterns that can be learned and anticipated; modeling when and why people step in enables agents to collaborate more effectively instead of over-autonomizing or asking needless confirmations.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a principled framework for predicting and reasoning about human intervention during autonomous web task execution, reducing harmful autonomous decisions and unnecessary human queries.
method: Collect and annotate CowCorpus — a dataset of web task traces with labeled human intervention points and contextual signals.
Train supervised sequence/prediction models that use agent state, task context, and uncertainty cues to predict likely intervention moments and types.
Analyze intervention causes and outcomes to derive policies for when agents should defer, query, or act autonomously.
impact: Provides practitioners with data-driven tools to build collaborative web agents that defer or query at the right moments, improving reliability and user trust. Enables evaluation benchmarks and design guidelines for human-in-the-loop web automation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: web agent interacting with pages, decision points highlighted where interventions occur
Bar/stacked chart: distribution of intervention types and frequencies from CowCorpus
Sequence timeline: example task trace showing model-predicted vs. actual intervention points
Icon set: causes of intervention (uncertainty, ambiguity, preference mismatch, safety) mapped to agent actions (defer, ask, act)
paper_title: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
paper_authors: Faria Huq, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Zhanqiu Guo, Venu Arvind Arangarajan, Tianyue Ou
